# Welcome to my GEO712 Repository!

The goal of this repository is to practice using GitHub, as part of my course: [Reproducible Research Workflow](https://github.com/paezha/Reproducible-Research-Workflow/).

***

# Repository Structure

- Folder: **Parent**
  - _Includes several setup files and the markdown files for the "homepage" *README*._
  - Folder: **assets**
    - _Auxiliary images and data added as part of the assignment due 10/28._
    - _Initially populated with sample data/results figures from my research on tropical forest biomass growth trajectories, using an Ecoregion in Western Africa._
  - Folder: **easter-egg**
    - _Created by Antonio as a contributor, including markdown and results for generating Tanaka contours of Mount Fuji._
  - Folder: **notes**
    - _Notes I keep for myself each assignment/class, organized with the naming conventions: **AssignmentNotes_MM-DD** and **ClassNotes_MM-DD** respectively._
    - Folder: **Rmd_Files**
      - _Keeping the more "back-end" files separate for simple navigation._
  - Folder: **renv**
    - _Includes several setup files for a reproducible environment._

# About Me

## Academic History
- BA Environmental Studies: Lewis & Clark College (2026)
- MSc Earth & Environmental Sciences: McMaster University (In Progress)

## Main Research Interests
My principal areas of interest include:

- Tropical and coastal ecology

- Spatial analysis/remote sensing/GIS

- Carbon sequestration

At McMaster, I work with Dr. Alemu Gonsamo's _Remote Sensing Lab._ My research here centers on **how tropical forests recover their biomass following stand-replacing disturbances.** My approach uses _space-for-time substitution,_ which means I quantify biomass from one recent year, but across forests that were disturbed in different years. That way, I can find a relationship between forest age and biomass, essentially finding the rate of recovery over time.

Specifically, I am recording aboveground biomass estimations from spaceborne LiDAR data, made available by the _GEDI L4A_ product, and relating this to forest loss data from the _Global Forest Change_ project.

### Favorite Equation
_NDMI = (NIR-SWIR) / (NIR+SWIR)_

Where _NDMI_ is the Normalized Difference Moisture Index, _NIR_ is near infrared reflectance, and _SWIR_ is shortwave infrared reflectance.
